name: Sikafloor-359 N
paste:
SIKAFLOOR®-359 N: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikafloor®-359 N, April 2023, Version 02.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/t/sikafloor_-359_n.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikafloor®-359 N where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 02.01).
1.2 Product description. Sikafloor®-359 N is a two part tough-elastic, coloured, non-yellowing, polyurethane seal coat.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikafloor®-359 N may only be used by experienced professionals.
    - Abrasion resistant seal coat with high mechanical resistance for broadcast systems with crack-bridging properties in industrial flooring
    - Particularly suitable for car park decks, ramps and warehouses etc.
    - Aircraft Hangers and other industrial applications
    - As a UV stable Coating to be applied over many Sikafloor Epoxy and Polyurethange flooring systems
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.10.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikafloor®-359 N
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: 2-part PUR tough-elastic coloured seal coat
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals / certificates.
    - Synthetic resin screed material according to EN 13813:2002, Declaration of Performance 02080104002500000011008, certified by notified factory production control certification body 0921, and provided with the CE marking.
    - Coating for surface protection of concrete according to EN 1504-2:2004, Declaration of Performance 02080104002500000011008, certified by notified factory production control certification body 0921, and provided with the CE marking.
    - Certified as part of the Surface Protection System OS 11a according to DIN EN 1504-2 and DIN V 18026.
    - Certified as part of the Surface Protection System OS 11b according to DIN EN 1504-2 and DIN V 18026.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - EN 13813:2002: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - EN 1504-2:2004: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - DIN EN 1504-2: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - DIN EN ISO 2811-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Density (p.2).
    - DIN 53 505: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Abrasion resistance (p.2); Technical Information > Shore D Hardness (p.2).
    - EN 13892-8: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Tough-elastic
    - Good mechanical and chemical resistance
    - Watertight
    - Good opacity
    - Non-yellowing
    - Matt finish
    - Easy application
    - Slip resistant surface possible
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Polyurethane
2.6 Appearance and colour.
    | Resin - part A | coloured, liquid |
    | Hardener - part B | transparent, liquid |
    | Almost unlimited choice of colour shades. |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
2.7 Density.
    | Part A | ~ 1.67 kg/l |
    | Part B | ~ 1.05 kg/l |
    | Mixed resin | ~ 1.45 kg/l |
    | All Density values at +23°C |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (DIN EN ISO 2811-1)
2.8 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Solid content by mass: ~85 %
    - Solid content by volume: ~85 %
    - Shore D Hardness: ~52 (7 days / +23 °C) (DIN 53 505)
    - Abrasion resistance: 160 mg (CS 10/1000/1000) (7 days / +23 °C) (DIN 53 505)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: > 1.5 N/mm² (failure in concrete) (EN 13892-8)
    - Chemical resistance: Resistant to many chemicals. Contact Sika technical service for specific information. Resiistant to Skydrol in a spill scenario: Spills should be cleanded immediatly to avoid potencial staining:
2.9 Systems. Please refer to the System Data Sheet of:
    | Sikafloor® MultiFlex PB-32 UV | Broadcast unicolour high perform- |
    | ance polyurethane floor covering with UV sealer |
    | Sikafloor® MultiFlex PB-55 UV | Broadcast unicolour high perform- |
    | ance polyurethane floor covering over elastic membrane with UV sealer |
    | Sikafloor® MultiFlex PB-56 UV | Broadcast unicolour high perform- |
    | ance polyurethane elastic membrane with UV sealer |
    (System build-up table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows. Refer to the data sheet (page 2) for the layout.)
2.10 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Shelf life: 12 months from date of production
    - Storage conditions: The product must be stored properly in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging, in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +30 °C.
2.11 Packaging.
    | Part A | 25.35 kg containers |
    | Part B | 7.15 kg containers |
    | Part A+B | 32.5 kg ready to mix units |

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 02.01) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality / pre-treatment. The surface must be clean, dry and free of all contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, coatings and surface treatments, etc. All dust, loose and friable material must be completely removed from all surfaces before application of the product, preferably by vacuum. Pull off strength shall not be less than 1.5 N/mm². If in doubt apply a test area first.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 02.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: Part A : part B = 78 : 22 (by weight)
    - Consumption: ~0.7–0.9 kg/m²/layer. Please refer to the respective System Data Sheet.
4.3 Pot Life.
    | Temperature | Time |
    | +10 °C | ~ 40 minutes |
    | +20 °C | ~ 25 minutes |
    | +30 °C | ~ 15 minutes |
4.4 Curing time. Before applying Sikafloor®-359 N on Sikafloor®-375/ -350 N/ -326/ -261 broadcast allow:
    | Substrate temperature | Minimum | Maximum |
    | +10 °C | 24 hours | * |
    | +20 °C | 12 hours | * |
    | +30 °C | 6 hours | * |
    Times are approximate and will be affected by changing ambient conditions particularly temperature and relative humidity.
    * Not applicable as the product will be applied on the structured surface provided by the quartz sand.
4.5 Applied product ready for use.
    | Temperature | Foot traffic | Light traffic | Full cure |
    | +10 °C | ~ 48 hours | ~ 5 days | ~ 10 days |
    | +20 °C | ~ 24 hours | ~ 3 days | ~ 7 days |
    | +30 °C | ~ 16 hours | ~ 2 days | ~ 3 days |
    Note: Times are approximate and will be affected by changing ambient conditions
4.6 Mixing.
    - Prior to mixing, stir part A mechanically. When all of part B has been added to part A, mix continuously for 2 minutes until a uniform mix has been achieved.
    - For the addition of quartz sand: When parts A and B have been mixed, add the quartz sand 0.1 - 0.3 mm and mix for a further 2 minutes until a uniform mix has been achieved. To ensure thorough mixing pour materials into another container and mix again to achieve a consistent mix. Over mixing must be avoided to minimise air entrainment.
4.7 Mixing - Mixing Tools. Sikafloor®-359 N must be thoroughly mixed using a low speed electric stirrer (300 - 400 rpm) or other suitable equipment.
4.8 Application. Prior to application, confirm substrate moisture content, relative humidity and dew point. As a seal coat, the product can be applied by squeegee and then back-rolled (crosswise) with a short-piled roller.
4.9 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with Thinner C immediately after use. Hardened and/or cured material can only be removed mechanically.
4.10 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Freshly applied Sikafloor®-359 N must be protected from damp, condensation and water for at least 24 hours.
    - Sikafloor®-359 N applied at different thicknesses can lead to different degrees of matt finish.
    - If heating is required do not use gas, oil, paraffin or other fossil fuel heaters, these produce large quantities of both CO2 and H2O water vapour, which may adversely affect the finish. For heating use only electric powered warm air blower systems.
    - The incorrect assessment and treatment of cracks may lead to a reduced service life and reflective cracking.
    - For exact colour matching, ensure Sikafloor®-359 N in each area is applied from the same control batch numbers.
4.11 Further information - Substrate Quality & Preparation. Please refer to Sika Method Statement: “EVALUATION AND PREPARATION OF SURFACES FOR FLOORING SYSTEMS”.
4.12 Further information - Application Instructions.
    - Please refer to Sika Method Statement: “MIXING & APPLICATION OF FLOORING SYSTEMS”.
    - Maintenance
    - Please refer to “Sikafloor®- CLEANING REGIME”.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +10 °C min. / +30 °C max.
5.3 Relative air humidity. 80 % r.h. max.
5.4 Dew point. Beware of condensation! The substrate and uncured floor must be at least 3 °C above dew point to reduce the risk of condensation or blooming on the floor finish.
5.5 Substrate temperature. +10 °C min. / +30 °C max.
5.6 Substrate moisture content. < 4 % pbw moisture content. Test method: Sika®-Tramex meter, CM - measurement or oven-dry-method. No rising moisture according to ASTM (Polyethylene-sheet).
5.7 Trials, test areas and compatibility checks stated by the manufacturer.
    - The surface must be clean, dry and free of all contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, coatings and surface treatments, etc. All dust, loose and friable material must be completely removed from all surfaces before application of the product, preferably by vacuum. Pull off strength shall not be less than 1.5 N/mm². If in doubt apply a test area first.
5.8 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Density: Part A | ~ 1.67 kg/l; Part B | ~ 1.05 kg/l; Mixed resin | ~ 1.45 kg/l; All Density values at +23°C (DIN EN ISO 2811-1)
    - Shore D Hardness: ~52 (7 days / +23 °C) (DIN 53 505)
    - Abrasion resistance: 160 mg (CS 10/1000/1000) (7 days / +23 °C) (DIN 53 505)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: > 1.5 N/mm² (failure in concrete) (EN 13892-8)
5.9 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.10 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikafloor®-359 N, April 2023, Version 02.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/t/sikafloor_-359_n.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikafloor®-359 N Part B, version 23/07/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/5/sds-sikafloor-359npartb.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikafloor®-359 N Part A, version 24/07/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/9/sds-sikafloor-359nparta.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
